**[<<< Series 3](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWho2006CSTheRunawayBride "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWho2006CSTheRunawayBride")** | **[2009 Specials >>>](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS30E14TheNextDoctor "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS30E14TheNextDoctor")**

Silence in the Library
----------------------

![Image 1: Doctor Who S30 E8 "Silence in the Library" Recap](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/SilenceInTheLibrary_1161.jpg)

Written by [Steven Moffat](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/StevenMoffat "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/StevenMoffat")  
Directed by Euros Lyn  
**Production code:** 4.9  
**Air date:** 31 May 2008  
**Part 1 of 2**

_"Daleks — aim for the eyestalk. Sontarans — back of the neck. Vashta Nerada..._ _**run**_. _Just run."_

— **The Doctor**

[The One With…](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/JustForFun/TheOneWith "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/JustForFun/TheOneWith") _[Monty Python's Big Red Book](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/MontyPython "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/MontyPython")_, the first appearance of "[Spoilers](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Spoiler "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Spoiler")", and the one where hiding behind the sofa stops being an effective deterrent.

[Steven Moffat](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/StevenMoffat "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/StevenMoffat") wrote the story after being promoted to head writer of _[Doctor Who](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Series/DoctorWho "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Series/DoctorWho")_ from series 5 onwards. An early version of the Library itself was introduced by Moffat in his 1996 short story "[Continuity Errors](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Literature/ContinuityErrors "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Literature/ContinuityErrors")", the first _Doctor Who_ story he ever wrote.

True to Moffat form, the episodes were nominated for a [Hugo Award](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/MediaNotes/HugoAward "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/MediaNotes/HugoAward"), but they lost out to [a certain sing-along blog](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/WebVideo/DoctorHorriblesSingAlongBlog "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/WebVideo/DoctorHorriblesSingAlongBlog").

["Silence in the Library" was broadcast with a special warning to parents: don't let your kids watch it late at night.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NightmareFuel "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NightmareFuel")

* * *

Somewhere in a very ordinary house, a little girl has schizophrenic visions of a library: huge and beautiful and — best of all — just for her. That is, until the Doctor and Donna show up. The little girl's father and her therapist (Dr. Moon) try to make sense of it all.

The Doctor's psychic paper has brought him to the biggest library in the universe, the size of a planet, and it's unsettlingly empty. Also, there's a little -x- kiss in the psychic message. But bio-scans claim that the Library is not actually empty at all, so where _is_ everyone? And where's the little girl? And why is a robot with a human face telling them to count the shadows?

The Doctor spots a security camera and uses his sonic screwdriver to scan it. The little girl screams in agony at the sound. The Doctor realises that the camera is sentient, and he and the girl have a rudimentary conversation through its display. Both are quite confused at this.

A team of 52nd century archaeologists show up, one of whom, Professor River Song, knows the Doctor _very_ well. Though [what kind of](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E5FleshAndStone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E5FleshAndStone") [connection they have](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS32E8LetsKillHitler "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS32E8LetsKillHitler") [is not revealed... yet](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS32E13TheWeddingOfRiverSong "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS32E13TheWeddingOfRiverSong"). She greets him with a loving "Hello, sweetie!", then appears a bit miffed when he doesn't return the sentiment. River is mysterious, but definitely not a [Mysterious Waif](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MysteriousWaif "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MysteriousWaif"): she's mature, snarky and able to take care of herself.

The little girl has watched much of that on her TV, even briefly talking with River and the Doctor through her screen.

River pulls the Doctor aside to catch up and compare diaries, to see how their personal timelines are at the moment. The Doctor just stares at her blankly. Actually, _[David Tennant](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/DavidTennant "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/DavidTennant")_ just stares at her blankly, because [Steven Moffat](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/StevenMoffat "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/StevenMoffat") [refused to tell him what was going on](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EnforcedMethodActing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EnforcedMethodActing"). River is appropriately horrified when she realises that the Doctor has never met _her_. To him, this is their very first meeting. To her, he looks too young, too inexperienced, too happy. He's not _her_ Doctor yet. She also realises that, due to their timelines, the first time the Doctor meets her will be the last time she meets him.

No time to dwell on that, though, as the Library is infested with flesh-eating shadows: Vashta Nerada. They're not every shadow... [but they could be any shadow](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PrimalFear "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PrimalFear"). They live on any planet that provides meat. Yes, [including Earth](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ParanoiaFuel "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ParanoiaFuel").

River Song turns out to have a sonic screwdriver, much to the Doctor's surprise.

River finds out who Donna is, and gives her a look of utmost pity. Donna's future doesn't look too happy. But River knows that she shouldn't spoil the ending.

The shadows kill one of the party, Miss Evangelista, stripping her flesh and leaving only a skeleton. The sound system in her protective suit is linked to her neural pathways and echoes her voice long after she's died, which is appropriately terrifying. Another is killed, with the Vashta Nerada animating his suit and chasing everyone else through the blacked-out hallways.

Dr. Moon asks the little girl's dad if he can talk to her alone for a moment. Because he needs to tell her something very important:

**Dr. Moon:** The real world is a _lie_, and your nightmares are **real**.

The Doctor tries to send Donna back to the TARDIS, using the teleporter in the Library's [little shop](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RunningGag "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RunningGag"). But she is yanked out of existence — screaming and mid-teleport — to take her place among the Library's robot servants with real people's faces.

The Doctor then gets a better look at River's screwdriver, and discovers it looks an awful lot like his own. Then he realizes that the TARDIS didn't signal him that someone teleported aboard, and when attempting to find Donna discovers that she's become one of the robots with human faces, to his horror, as the shadows close in...

* * *

Tropes:
-------

*   [Action Prologue](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ActionPrologue "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ActionPrologue"): The little girl apparently experiences one through her dreams, as the Doctor and Donna board themselves up in some kind of library room. Also [In Medias Res](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InMediasRes "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InMediasRes"), as we see the same scene again from the Doctor and Donna's point of view later in the episode.
*   [Adventurer Archaeologist](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdventurerArchaeologist "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdventurerArchaeologist"): _Professor_ River Song and her crew are exploring a very dangerous place.
*   [Apocalypse How](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ApocalypseHow "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ApocalypseHow"): An interesting case in that the Library is a planet which is technically an entirely-artificial futuristic building, and all 4,022 of its immediate (and obviously non-native) visitors disappeared off its surface in a sort-of [Class 3a](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/ApocalypseHow/Class3A "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/ApocalypseHow/Class3A") absolute [Depopulation Bomb](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DepopulationBomb "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DepopulationBomb"), leaving only the swarms of Vashta Nerada while the planet was sealed off. The next episode explains how and why the Depopulation Bomb happened.
*   [Apocalyptic Log](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ApocalypticLog "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ApocalypticLog"): The messages on the computer at the beginning record the last moments before the shadows arrived.
*   [Big Bad](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigBad "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigBad"): The Vashta Narada.
*   [Brainless Beauty](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrainlessBeauty "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrainlessBeauty"): Miss Evangelista is well aware that she's stupid and also pretty."My dad told me I had the IQ of plankton and I was pleased."
    
*   [Broken Record](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrokenRecord "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrokenRecord"):
    *   "Reminder: The Library has been breached. Others are coming. Reminder: The Library has been breached. Others are coming. Reminder: The Library has breached. Others are coming."
    *   "Hey, who turned out the lights?"
    *   "Donna Noble has left the Library. Donna Noble has been saved."
*   [Comm Links](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CommLinks "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CommLinks"): They happen to be capable of catching the last thoughts of their users, though they quickly turn into a [Broken Record](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrokenRecord "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrokenRecord").
*   [Continuity Nod](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ContinuityNod "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ContinuityNod"):
    *   "[Squareness](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS27E9TheEmptyChild "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS27E9TheEmptyChild") [gun](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS27E10TheDoctorDances "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS27E10TheDoctorDances")!" [Steven Moffat](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/StevenMoffat "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/StevenMoffat") has confirmed that it's Jack's gun, left in the TARDIS at the end of Series 1.
    *   The Little Shop in the Library, which the Doctor is delighted over, is a call back to "[New Earth](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS28E1NewEarth "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS28E1NewEarth")" and "[Smith and Jones](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS29E1SmithAndJones "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS29E1SmithAndJones")".
    *   A [promotional image![Image 2](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/external_link.gif)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/tardis/images/e/e6/Silence_books_promo.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20210613175814) reveals that the Library has copies of _[A Journal of](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS29E8HumanNature "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS29E8HumanNature") [Impossible Things](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS29E9TheFamilyOfBlood "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS29E9TheFamilyOfBlood")_, _[The French Revolution](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS1E1AnUnearthlyChild "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS1E1AnUnearthlyChild")_, _[Origins of the Universe](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS17E1DestinyOfTheDaleks "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS17E1DestinyOfTheDaleks")_ by Oolun Colluphid, _[Everest in Easy Stages](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS17E3TheCreatureFromThePit "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS17E3TheCreatureFromThePit")_, [the TARDIS instruction manual](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS17E5TheHornsOfNimon "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS17E5TheHornsOfNimon"), _[Black Orchid](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS19E5BlackOrchid "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS19E5BlackOrchid")_, and _[Understanding Telebiogenesis](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS19E1Castrovalva "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS19E1Castrovalva")_.
    *   The Doctor says that if he doesn't get back to the TARDIS after five hours, Emergency Program One will activate and send Donna back home for her safety. This is the same TARDIS feature that the Ninth Doctor used to send Rose back home to protect her from the incoming Dalek fleet in Satellite Five in "[The Parting of the Ways](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS27E13ThePartingOfTheWays "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS27E13ThePartingOfTheWays")".
*   [Conversational Troping](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ConversationalTroping "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ConversationalTroping"): The Doctor and Donna discuss how [Time Travel](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TimeTravel "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TimeTravel") can lead to [Spoilers](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Spoiler "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Spoiler") about life.
*   [Corrupt Corporate Executive](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CorruptCorporateExecutive "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CorruptCorporateExecutive"): Lux seems to be one of these, [at least until the next episode](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS30E9ForestOfTheDead "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS30E9ForestOfTheDead").
*   [Creepy Monotone](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CreepyMonotone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CreepyMonotone"): "[Run. For god's sake, run. The Library has sealed itself. We can't. Oh. They're here. Agh. Slaugh. Snik. Message ends.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ApocalypticLog "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ApocalypticLog") [Please switch off your mobile comm units](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoTalkingOrPhonesWarning "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoTalkingOrPhonesWarning") [for the comfort of other readers.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DissonantSerenity "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DissonantSerenity")"
*   [Cutting the Knot](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CuttingTheKnot "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CuttingTheKnot"): The Doctor is trying to figure out how to get a door open with his sonic screwdriver ("It doesn't do wood?!"). Donna just kicks it open.**The Doctor:** Nice door skills, Donna.  
    **Donna:** Yeah, well, you know. Boyfriends. Sometimes you need the element of surprise.
    
*   [Darkness Equals Death](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DarknessEqualsDeath "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DarknessEqualsDeath"): Quite literally; stand in the darkness, in the shadows, and you will be eaten.
*   [Did I Say That Out Loud](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DidISayThatOutLoud "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DidISayThatOutLoud"): Donna is visibly bothered when she realizes it sounds like she thinks the Doctor is attractive.**The Doctor:** Oh, _I'm_ [Pretty Boy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PrettyBoy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PrettyBoy")!  
    **Donna:** YES! Oh... that came out a bit quick...  
    **The Doctor:** Pretty?  
    **Donna:** Eh. _\[shrugs\]_
    
*   [Distress Call](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DistressCall "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DistressCall"): Sent out a hundred years ago, but the defences around the planet were so good they only just were able to get through.
*   [Dissonant Serenity](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DissonantSerenity "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DissonantSerenity"): The first node gives a message in a very calm, measured tone. "There follows a brief message from the head librarian for your urgent attention. It has been edited for tone and content by a Felleman Lux automated decency filter. Run. For god's sake, run. Nowhere is safe. The library has sealed itself. We can't... oh, they're here. Argh. Slog. Snick. Message ends."
*   [The Ditz](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheDitz "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheDitz"): Miss Evangelista. On the ship to the Library, she mistook an escape pod for the bathroom. _Twice_.
*   [Don't Ask, Just Run](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DontAskJustRun "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DontAskJustRun"): "Daleks — aim for the eyestalk. Sontarans — back of the neck. Vashta Nerada... _run_. Just run."
*   [Due to the Dead](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DueToTheDead "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DueToTheDead"): Proper Dave asks if they can shut off Miss Evangelista's comm unit. River shuts him down hard.
*   [The End of the World as We Know It](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheEndOfTheWorldAsWeKnowIt "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheEndOfTheWorldAsWeKnowIt"): One hundred years before the episode begins, everyone on the library world mysteriously disappeared, and the planet was sealed off.
*   [Escape Pod](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EscapePod "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EscapePod"): On the voyage to the Library, Miss Evangelista mistook one of the ship's escape pods for the bathroom _twice_, requiring them to turn back for her both times.
*   [Foreshadowing](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Foreshadowing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Foreshadowing"):
    *   The Doctor makes a point of mentioning that the books are all new editions printed specially for the Library.
    *   River mentions the [crash of the](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E4TheTimeOfAngels "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E4TheTimeOfAngels") _[Byzantium](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E5FleshAndStone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E5FleshAndStone")_ while checking her diary.
    *   She also mentions that the Doctor created some rules for their relationship — one of which is "No peeking in River's diary".
    *   "4022 people _saved_."
    *   Proper Dave flinches visibly when the Doctor describes the Vashta Nerada's feeding habits and adjusts his suit a little bit. Guess who's next on the menu.
    *   River's reaction when she discovers Donna's identity, and Donna's sense of alarm that River is from the Doctor's future but hadn't met _her_.
    *   River's controlled anger when she says she'd like to meet the thing that killed Miss Evangelista, hinting that she is a [Good Is Not Soft](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoodIsNotSoft "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoodIsNotSoft") [Action Girl](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ActionGirl "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ActionGirl").
*   [The Gadfly](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheGadfly "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheGadfly"):
    *   River, starting as she means to go on, tells her boss to put his helmet on because she doesn't fancy him.
    *   The Doctor points and laughs at archaeologists.
*   [Get Out!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GetOut "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GetOut"):**River:** Hello, sweetie.  
    **The Doctor:** Get out.  
    **Donna:** Doctor...  
    **The Doctor:** All of you, turn around, get back in your rocket and fly away. Tell your grandchildren you came to the Library and lived. They won't believe you.
    
*   [Ghost Planet](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GhostPlanet "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GhostPlanet"): Ghost planet-sized library.
*   [Great Big Library of Everything](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GreatBigLibraryOfEverything "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GreatBigLibraryOfEverything"): Well, it's the size of a _planet_ and has copies of every book ever printed, so yes.
*   [Have We Met Yet?](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HaveWeMetYet "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HaveWeMetYet"): River appears to know the Doctor very well, but the Doctor himself doesn't know who she is (yet).
*   [Hypocritical Humour](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HypocriticalHumour "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HypocriticalHumour"):
    
    *   The Doctor berates Lux that he doesn't want one man's pride to kill everyone in the room. River says ["Then why don't you sign his contract?"](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DoubleStandard "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DoubleStandard") Then she admits she hadn't signed hers either.
    *   Lux is annoyed that Other Dave is taking orders from the Doctor even as the Doctor yells "Torch!" and Lux holds it up for the Doctor to take without even thinking about it.
    
    **Doctor:** Spooky, isn't it?
    
*   [I Lied](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ILied "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ILied"):
    *   River. "I lied. I'm always lying."
    *   And this gem from the Doctor:**Donna:** Doctor, we haven't got any helmets.  
        **The Doctor:** Yeah, but we're safe anyway.  
        **Donna:** How are we safe?  
        **The Doctor:** We're not. That was a clever lie to shut you up.
        
    *   Followed almost immediately by this one:**Donna:** I'm not leaving...  
        **The Doctor:** Donna, [let me explain!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MrExposition "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MrExposition")  
        _\[The Doctor immediately teleports Donna into the TARDIS\]_  
        **The Doctor:** Ah, that's how you do it!
        
*   [Irony](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Irony "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Irony"): A family named "light" in Latinnote  accidentally created the most dangerous concentration of _darkness_ in the universe.
*   [Interface with a Familiar Face](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InterfaceWithAFamiliarFace "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InterfaceWithAFamiliarFace"): A common habit in the 51st century, it seems. The Doctor equates it to donating a park bench.
*   [Invincible Boogeymen](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InvincibleBoogeymen "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InvincibleBoogeymen"): The Vashta Nerada. They seem only marginally [Weakened by the Light](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WeakenedByTheLight "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WeakenedByTheLight"), as it slows them down rather than actually harming or stopping them. When asked how to deal with the Vashta Nerada, the Doctor lampshades this trope by listing off weaknesses of various monsters, before adding "Vashta Nerada... run. Just run."
*   [Jerkass](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Jerkass "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Jerkass"): Mr. Lux is rude, unhelpful and self-centered... [supposedly.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS30E9ForestOfTheDead "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS30E9ForestOfTheDead")
*   [Jerkass Realization](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JerkassRealization "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JerkassRealization"): When the remnants of Miss Evangelista's consciousness request to talk to Donna because she was the only one who showed her any kindness, her fellow crewmates are clearly reflecting on their bullying treatment of her when she was alive and guiltily coming to this uncomfortable realization.
*   [Late to the Tragedy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LateToTheTragedy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LateToTheTragedy"): Played both straight and inverted. The Doctor arrives 100 years too late to the Library, but also arrives too early, since River had expected a later incarnation of the Doctor to show up.
*   [Leaning on the Fourth Wall](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LeaningOnTheFourthWall "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LeaningOnTheFourthWall"): Spoilers!
*   [Living Shadow](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LivingShadow "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LivingShadow"): The Vashta Nerada are the things in the dark and any shadow.
*   [Madness Mantra](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MadnessMantra "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MadnessMantra"):
    *   "Hey, who turned out the lights?"
    *   "Donna Noble has left the library. Donna Noble has been saved."
*   [Mind Screw](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MindScrew "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MindScrew"): The whole girl in therapy/the Doctor in the Library flip-flopping.
*   [Names to Run Away from Really Fast](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NamesToRunAwayFromReallyFast "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NamesToRunAwayFromReallyFast"): "Vashta Nerada" sounds threatening even before it's translated as "The Shadows That Melt the Flesh".
*   [No Bisexuals](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoBisexuals "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoBisexuals"): Averted. River openly admits to fancying everyone on the archaeological team save Mr. Lux. Since it's the 52nd century, when humans have developed new attitudes towards such things, no one comments on it. That and it'll later be implied to be a genetic trait.
*   [No Name Given](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoNameGiven "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoNameGiven"): "The girl" and "Dad".
*   [Non-Malicious Monster](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NonMaliciousMonster "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NonMaliciousMonster"): [Played With](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PlayedWith "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PlayedWith") in this case. The Doctor says that Vashta Nerada are normally benign and live off roadkill. The aggressiveness of this batch is highly unusual. ![Image 3](https://tvtropes.org/images/article-hreficon-ymmv.png)[Until you realize that the Vashta Nerada on this particular planet are essentially starving after a century of isolation from regular food sources](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FridgeHorror "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FridgeHorror").
*   [Noodle Incident](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoodleIncident "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoodleIncident"):
    *   Donna's explanation for her skills in kicking in doors make you wonder what kind of ex-boyfriends she's had to require the "element of surprise".
    *   While checking her diary, River asks the Doctor if he's done the "picnic at Asgard" or the "[crash of the](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E4TheTimeOfAngels "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E4TheTimeOfAngels") _[Byzantium](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E5FleshAndStone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS31E5FleshAndStone")_". The latter is now a [Resolved Noodle Incident](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ResolvedNoodleIncident "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ResolvedNoodleIncident").
*   ["No Talking or Phones" Warning](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoTalkingOrPhonesWarning "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoTalkingOrPhonesWarning"): The terminal that tells the Doctor and Donna the messages from before the Library was sealed ends with an emotionless request to switch off their mobile comm units for the comfort of other readers.
*   [Nothing Is Scarier](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NothingIsScarier "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NothingIsScarier"): The Vashta Nerada are _almost, almost_ invisible. You can't see them — and if you do, you're already dead or something's gone wrong. You can only see the results.
*   [Not Now, Kiddo](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NotNowKiddo "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NotNowKiddo"): Miss Evangelista getting blown off when the panel opens up.
*   [Oh, Crap!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OhCrap "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OhCrap"):
    *   The Doctor realizes what happened to Miss Evangelista before the rest of them. The others catch on when River tries to call her over comms and hears the echo coming from Evangelista's suit.
    *   "[I'm sorry. I am so, so sorry.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Catchphrase "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Catchphrase") But you've got two shadows."
    *   "Hey! Who turned out the lights?"
    *   "The real world is a lie, and your nightmares are real."
    *   River gets one when she finally realizes the Doctor has no idea who she is.
    *   The Doctor gets one when River pulls out her own sonic screwdriver.
*   [One-Steve Limit](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OneSteveLimit "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OneSteveLimit"): Averted with Proper Dave and Other Dave.
*   [Pretty Boy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PrettyBoy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PrettyBoy"): Yes, you, Doctor.
*   [Primal Fear](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PrimalFear "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PrimalFear"): Discussed by the Doctor.**The Doctor:** Almost every species in the universe has an irrational fear of the dark. But they're wrong: it's not irrational. It's Vashta Nerada.  
    **Donna:** What's Vashta Nerada?  
    **The Doctor:** [It's what's in the dark](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LivingShadow "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LivingShadow"). It's what's _always_ in the dark.
    
*   [Remember the New Guy?](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RememberTheNewGuy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RememberTheNewGuy"): Inverted with River Song, who walks up to the Doctor and begins chatting with him as if they're old friends. The Doctor, however, has never met her before — turns out that, thanks to time-travel, he's meeting her out of sequence.
*   [Rock Beats Laser](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RockBeatsLaser "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RockBeatsLaser"): The sonic screwdriver "doesn't do wood", to Donna's incredulousness.
*   [Running Gag](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RunningGag "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RunningGag"): The Doctor spots a little shop. He loves a little shop.
*   [Sacrificial Lamb](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SacrificialLamb "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SacrificialLamb"): Miss Evangelista. Notably, her "data ghost" runs out of power a lot faster than everyone else's, but also takes a lot longer than everyone else's to degrade into [repetitive utterances](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MadnessMantra "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MadnessMantra") (seemingly just to establish a plot point [and traumatize Donna](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TraumaCongaLine "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TraumaCongaLine")).
*   [Sacrificial Lion](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SacrificialLion "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SacrificialLion"): Proper Dave. His death establishes that the Vashta Nerada _will_ eat you if you touch them, and that [they can move perfectly-sealed suits almost as well as muscles](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PeopleInRubberSuits "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PeopleInRubberSuits").
*   [San Dimas Time](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SanDimasTime "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SanDimasTime"): You could usually count on everyone the Doctor meets remembering events in the same order; this is one of the first episodes to play with that.
*   [Saying Sound Effects Out Loud](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SayingSoundEffectsOutLoud "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SayingSoundEffectsOutLoud"): The computer terminal that recites the [Apocalyptic Log](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ApocalypticLog "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ApocalypticLog") in the Library's computers dispassionately reads the onomatopoeia as well.
*   [Schmuck Bait](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SchmuckBait "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SchmuckBait"): The conveniently-opened wall panel in the room where the Doctor's and River's parties first meet. And Miss Evangelista, of course, falls for it.
*   [Sci-Fi Writers Have No Sense of Scale](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SciFiWritersHaveNoSenseOfScale "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SciFiWritersHaveNoSenseOfScale"): The Universe's largest library, home to every written work ever and run by a powerful computer... can't count past one million million (ie a US and increasingly UK-adopted trillion or traditional UK billion (bi-million), which is probably why the episode phrases it unambiguously). A 64-bit integer in a modern computer can exceed that by a factor of about _18.5 million_. Possibly it's the life-scanner's sensitivity, not the Library's counting ability, which hit its limit at that point.
*   [Self-Plagiarism](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SelfPlagiarism "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SelfPlagiarism"): The idea of the Doctor in the biggest library in the universe first appeared in Moffat's short story "Continuity Errors".
*   [Serial Escalation](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SerialEscalation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SerialEscalation"): Scaring viewers into hiding behind the sofa was no longer enough. This is the episode that decides to _scare them out_.
*   [Single-Biome Planet](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SingleBiomePlanet "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SingleBiomePlanet"): [Justified](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JustifiedTrope "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JustifiedTrope") — it's a purpose-built artificial planet, so the biome is "library".
*   [Spell My Name with a "The"](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SpellMyNameWithAThe "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SpellMyNameWithAThe"):**The Doctor:** The Library. So big it doesn't need a name, just a great big _the_.
    
*   [Spoiler](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Spoiler "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Spoiler"):
    *   River Song discusses how time travel to and from the future can create spoilers for _reality_, which is why it would be a very bad idea for the Doctor to read her journal containing "spoilers" about his future self.
    *   Also played with in a [Leaning on the Fourth Wall](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LeaningOnTheFourthWall "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LeaningOnTheFourthWall") kind of way in the "Next Time" trailer at the end of the episode: the clips combine the Doctor asking about CAL, River and the Doctor both saying "Spoilers", and the little girl screaming "[No! Don't tell! You mustn't tell!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/QuotesFitForATrailer "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/QuotesFitForATrailer")"
*   [Spooky Silent Library](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SpookySilentLibrary "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SpookySilentLibrary"): Murders by living shadows makes for "Silence in the Library". There was some catastrophe earlier and now the place is eerie.
*   [Stable Time Loop](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StableTimeLoop "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StableTimeLoop"): The Doctor only knows about the rule against diary-peeking because River told him about it.
*   [Stripped to the Bone](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StrippedToTheBone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StrippedToTheBone"): The Vashta Nerada don't eat bones, so the skeletons of their victims are all that's left behind.
*   [Sunday is Boring](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SundayIsBoring "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SundayIsBoring"): The Doctor says, "I never land \[the TARDIS\] on Sundays. Sundays are boring."
*   [Super-Speed](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SuperSpeed "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SuperSpeed"): The Vashta Nerada feed fast. Blink of an eye fast.
*   [Time-Travel Tense Trouble](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TimeTravelTenseTrouble "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TimeTravelTenseTrouble"): River has a bit of this talking about her history with the Doctor because she refers to past events that are his future. It gets confusing.
*   [Title Drop](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TitleDrop "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TitleDrop"): "A million million lifeforms... and silence in the Library..."
*   [Too Dumb to Live](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TooDumbToLive "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TooDumbToLive"): Miss Evangelista, and she's well aware of it, before she gets uploaded to the mainframe and gets a mental upgrade.
*   [Villain Ball](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VillainBall "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VillainBall"): The entire group is in shadowy lighting from the moment the archeologists arrive; in other words, the Vashta Nerada realistically could have eaten them _immediately_. Instead these starved microbes eat the archeologists one-by-one, [marking](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MarkedToDie "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MarkedToDie") their prey ahead of time (which the Doctor [hand-waves](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HandWave "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HandWave") as "how they hunt"), and waiting a seemingly-random amount of time before spontaneously [skeletizing](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StrippedToTheBone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StrippedToTheBone") their prey.
*   [Visible Boom Mic](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VisibleBoomMic "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VisibleBoomMic"): In the house, when CAL is telling her Dad that the phone is ringing while he's talking to Doctor Moon, a boom mic can be seen at the top centre of the shot where both Doctor Moon and Cal's Dad are talking.
*   [Wham Line](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhamLine "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhamLine"):
    
    *   Keep in mind this is a child psychologist talking to his patient:
    
    **Dr. Moon:** The real world is a _lie_, and your nightmares are _real._
    
    *   "I'm sorry, I'm so sorry, but you've got two shadows."
    *   "Donna Noble has left the library. Donna Noble has been saved."
*   [What the Hell, Hero?](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhatTheHellHero "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhatTheHellHero"): River delivers an understated but stinging one to the Doctor when he's quibbling about signing Mr. Lux's "personal experience contract":**Mr. Lux:** I'm protecting my family's pride.  
    **The Doctor:** Well, funny thing, Mr. Lux. I don't wanna see everyone in this room _dead_ because some idiot thinks his pride is more important.  
    **River:** Then why don't you sign his contract?
    
    *   Of course, she then says she also didn't sign it. ("I'm getting worse than you.")
*   [Whisper Reaction](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhisperReaction "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhisperReaction"): River Song whispers a word into the Doctor's ear, earning both a shocked look and his complete trust from that point on.
*   [Whole-Plot Reference](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WholePlotReference "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WholePlotReference"): Moffat is a big fan of _[The Time Traveler's Wife](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Literature/TheTimeTravelersWife "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Literature/TheTimeTravelersWife")_. River meeting the Doctor in the library _very_ much echoes Clare meeting Henry in a library in said novel.
*   [The Worm That Walks](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheWormThatWalks "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheWormThatWalks"): The Vashta Nerada, with the aid of a spacesuit and a skeleton, are able to walk around like a person, albeit awkwardly.
*   [Zombie Gait](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ZombieGait "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ZombieGait"): Suits possessed by a swarm have a clumsy walk.

* * *

* * *

### **Alternative Title(s):** Doctor Who NSS 4 E 8 Silence In The Library

*   [Doctor Who S30 E7 "The Unicorn and the Wasp"](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS30E7TheUnicornAndTheWasp)
*   [Recap/Doctor Who](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWho)
*   [Doctor Who S30 E9 "Forest of the Dead"](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Recap/DoctorWhoS30E9ForestOfTheDead)

**Ashildr** (also known as **Me**) is a [fictional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiction "Fiction") [character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_/(arts/) "Character (arts)") in the British [science fiction television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction_television "Science fiction television") series _[Doctor Who](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who "Doctor Who")_, portrayed by actress [Maisie Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maisie_Williams "Maisie Williams"). The character was introduced in the [ninth series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Who_/(series_9/) "Doctor Who (series 9)") episode "[The Girl Who Died](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Who_Died "The Girl Who Died")", before making a few more appearances during the series.

Ashildr, daughter of Ionhar (Ian Conningham), is introduced in "[The Girl Who Died](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Girl_Who_Died "The Girl Who Died")" (2015), where she is portrayed as a [Viking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking "Viking") puppet maker and [storyteller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storytelling "Storytelling"). When the militaristic [alien race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraterrestrials_in_fiction "Extraterrestrials in fiction") the Mire raid her village, Ashildr declares war between the village and ten of the Mire. As part of a battle plan devised by the alien [time traveller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_travel_in_fiction "Time travel in fiction") the [Twelfth Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_Doctor "Twelfth Doctor") ([Peter Capaldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Capaldi "Peter Capaldi")), Ashildr uses the technology inside one of the Mire's helmets to create an illusion to scare the Mire into a retreat. In doing so, she dies of heart failure, having been "used... up like a battery" by being connected to the Mire's machine. The Doctor's companion, [Clara Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clara_Oswald "Clara Oswald") ([Jenna Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Coleman "Jenna Coleman")), a time-travelling school teacher from 21st century England, persuades the Doctor to save her. He implants Ashildr with a Mire repair kit, bringing her back to life and making her functionally immortal, but he worries that there will be consequences and no companion for the immortal. He also gives her another piece of the same technology that brought her back to life before leaving.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-3)

In the following episode "[The Woman Who Lived](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Woman_Who_Lived "The Woman Who Lived")", the Doctor catches up with Ashildr in 1651 England after 800 years have passed for her. She has become a [highwayman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highwayman "Highwayman"), adopting the new name of "Me". While her body has become immortal, the human brain is physically insufficient to contain 800 years' worth of memories, which has evolved her personality: she has lived many lives under different personas, loved and lost many people, most of whom she cannot even remember clearly anymore. The only constant that remained was herself, leading to her developing the new name "Me" to refer to herself - she laments because everyone else she encounters is transient.

Having lived through many wars and suffered many losses, she plans to travel the galaxy with an alien Leonian called Leandro ([Ariyon Bakare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariyon_Bakare "Ariyon Bakare")) after the Doctor helps her retrieve an [amulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amulet "Amulet") called the Eyes of Hades, not knowing this will create a portal using the death of rival highwayman Sam Swift the Quick ([Rufus Hound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufus_Hound "Rufus Hound")). However, Leandro betrays Ashildr and, instead, summons a fleet of ships to attack [Earth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth "Earth"). Ashildr uses her spare piece of Mire medical technology to restore Sam's life and close the portal to Leandro's world. She promises the Doctor that she will watch over his [companions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Companion_/(Doctor_Who/) "Companion (Doctor Who)") on Earth, keeping them safe after they stop traveling with him. Shortly afterward, he spots her in the background of a photo on Clara's mobile phone taken in the 21st century.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-woman-1)

When the Doctor next encounters Ashildr in "[Face the Raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_the_Raven "Face the Raven")", she runs an alien refugee camp hidden in the heart of 21st century [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), having lured the Doctor in using Rigsy ([Joivan Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joivan_Wade "Joivan Wade")), an old acquaintance of his, as bait. In a reckless attempt at subverting Ashildr's plan, Clara takes on the death sentence given to Rigsy to buy more time, without realising that Ashildr cannot remove it once it is transferred to a new recipient, resulting in Clara's death. A now-remorseful Ashildr takes the Doctor's [TARDIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TARDIS "TARDIS") key, and teleports him to her collaborators, which was the plan all along,[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-4) who are revealed in "[Hell Bent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell_Bent_/(Doctor_Who/) "Hell Bent (Doctor Who)")" to be the Doctor's own race: the [Time Lords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Lords "Time Lords").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-hell_bent-5)

Before "Hell Bent", in "[Heaven Sent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaven_Sent_/(Doctor_Who/) "Heaven Sent (Doctor Who)")", the Doctor mentions that Ashildr/"Me" is going to destroy Gallifrey, because she is the "hybrid", echoing a prophecy related by [Davros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davros "Davros") in "[The Magician's Apprentice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Magician%27s_Apprentice_/(Doctor_Who/) "The Magician's Apprentice (Doctor Who)")" / "[The Witch's Familiar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Witch%27s_Familiar "The Witch's Familiar")".

In the ninth series finale "Hell Bent", the Doctor attempts to help Clara cheat death and runs away with her from the planet [Gallifrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallifrey "Gallifrey") (set roughly 14 billion years after Ashildr became immortal,[\[note 2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-6)) to the end of time itself (over 100 trillion years in the future [\[note 3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-7)). Here, Ashildr remains the last being in existence. She counsels the Doctor to stop his current course of action, for the sake of the universe, and so the Doctor and Clara submit themselves to have one of them wiped of their memories. The Doctor loses his memories of Clara, who returns him to Earth and reunites him with his TARDIS but departs with Ashildr for adventures of their own in a newly acquired TARDIS of their own – further extending Ashildr's lifespan. Clara promises Ashildr she will return to Gallifrey to face her death as history records, but not before seeing the universe in more depth first.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-hell_bent-5)

Casting and development
-----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashildr&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Casting and development")\]

Costumes worn by Ashildr/Me in "The Woman Who Lived", "Face the Raven" and "Hell Bent".

Head writer and [executive producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_producer "Executive producer") [Steven Moffat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Moffat "Steven Moffat") said about having Williams on _Doctor Who_, "We're thrilled to have Maisie Williams joining us on Doctor Who. It's not possible to say too much about who or what she's playing, but she is going to challenge the Doctor in very unexpected ways. This time he might just be out of his depth, and we know Maisie is going to give him exactly the right sort of hell."[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-BBCA-8)

Maisie Williams said about her role in _Doctor Who_, "I'm so excited to be working on Doctor Who as it's such a big and important part of British culture. I can't wait to meet the cast and crew and start filming, especially as we'll be shooting not too far from my home town."[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-BBCA-8)

When speaking about being in _Doctor Who_, Williams said about Peter Capaldi, "People say 'don't meet your idols as they never turn out to be who you want them to be'. That was completely not the case with Peter and he's been wonderful and really helpful on set."[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-9)

In 2016, Williams confirmed that she will not return to _Doctor Who_.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-10) The following year, she clarified that there was no reason she could not return in the future; she simply was not actively seeking to return for another appearance, and the show's producers hadn't asked her to return.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-11)

In a discussion about the episode "The Girl Who Died," Mike Reyes of _Cinema Blend_ said about Ashildr that "Sure enough, Ashildr's death and rebirth after fighting the Mire went from a happy ending to an ending that gave me pause. The Doctor has now officially created a functional immortal out of a normal human, and given how he's held up with such a life span, it looks like things are about to get scary."[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-12) Sam Warner of _[Digital Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Spy "Digital Spy")_ reported, when talking about the character's debut appearance, that "Opinion was mostly positive, though Ashildr hasn't convinced everyone just yet."[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-13)

Williams described her role in _Doctor Who_ as "every fan-boy's dream."[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-14) Liz Raftery of _[TV Guide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TV_Guide "TV Guide")_ described Williams's role as "highly anticipated," and Williams then went on to explain, "When you cross over to a different geeky fandom world, everyone's like, 'This is insane!'"[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-15)

In a review for the episode "The Girl Who Died," Rob Smedley of the website _CultBox_ referred to Williams's portrayal of Ashildr as "envied natural talent that ... lifts Ashildr above being convenience or novelty."[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-16) In reviewing the episode "The Woman Who Lived," Smedley stated that Williams, in her portrayal of Ashildr, had done "a terrific job of making the character feel like she’s lived lifetimes since we last saw her. Several hundred years of loss in just one week. It’s an even better, and inevitably more mature, performance than last Saturday."[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-17)

1.  **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_ref-2)** In "[The Woman Who Lived](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Woman_Who_Lived "The Woman Who Lived")" (2015), which is set in the year 1651, Ashildr mentions having had 800 years of adventure.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashildr#cite_note-woman-1)

10.content:
In the second episode of the latest series of [Doctor Who](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-release-date/), we've arrived at one of the most series' most anticipated episodes: Lux.

Featuring heavily in trailers for the season, Lux sees the Doctor and Belinda hit up 1952 Miami, where they come face to face with cartoon villain Mr Ring-a-Ding – played by [guest star Alan Cumming](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-season-15-date-confirmed-newsupdate/).

As well as Cumming, there are a few more guest appearances in the episode, with [Linus Roache](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lux-teaser-pics-newsupdate/), Lewis Cornay and another mysterious appearance for [Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-mrs-flood-anita-dobson-explained/).

But aside from that, who else is in the cast for this new episode? Keep reading to find out everything you need to know about the cast for Doctor Who season 15 episode 2, Lux.

**Who's in the cast of Doctor Who: Lux? Full list of characters in season 15 episode 2**
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The main cast for Doctor Who: Lux is as follows. Scroll on to find out more about the characters, plus where you may have seen the actors previously.

*   **Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor**
*   **Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra**
*   **Linus Roache as Reginald Pye**
*   **Alan Cumming as Mr Ring-a-Ding**
*   **Lewis Cornay as Logan Cheever**
*   **Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood**
*   **Millie O'Connell as Sunshine Sally**
*   **Cassius Hackforth as Tommy Lee**
*   **Lucy Thackeray as Renée Lowenstein**
*   **Jane Hancock as Helen Pye**
*   **Samir Arrian as Hassan**
*   **Bronte Barbe as Lizzie**
*   **Steph Lacey as Robyn**
*   **Ryan Speakman as Husband**
*   **Ian Shaw as Newsreader**
*   **William Meredith as Policeman**

**Ncuti Gatwa plays The Doctor**
--------------------------------

![Image 1: Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/516721-e921a8d.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is the Doctor?** The Doctor is a time traveller from Gallifrey, and the last of the Time Lords. He travels in space and time in the TARDIS. This version of the character is known as the Fifteenth Doctor, although we know there have been a number of additional incarnations.

**Where have I seen Ncuti Gatwa before?** Beyond his role as the Doctor, Gatwa is best known for his role as Eric Effiong in Sex Education, as well as for starring in [Barbie](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/barbie-review/) and [Masters of the Air](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/masters-of-the-air-release-date/).

**Varada Sethu plays Belinda Chandra**
--------------------------------------

![Image 2: Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/516712-e565295.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Belinda Chandra?** Belinda is a nurse from London who, in The Robot Revolution, was kidnapped by robots and flown into the stars on their rocket.

At the end of the episode she told the Doctor to take her home in the TARDIS, but he found himself unable to get back to that particular date, time and location. We don't yet know why this is the case, but we do know they will be trying to get back throughout the season.

**Where have I seen Varada Sethu before?** Sethu is no stranger for Doctor Who, having played Mundy Flynn in last season's episode 3, [Boom](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-varada-sethu-nods-boom-character-exclusive-newsupdate/). She is also known for her roles in series such as [Andor](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/andor-season-2-disney-plus-release-date/), Strike Back, Doctor Foster, Hard Sun and [Annika](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/nicola-walker-annika-fourth-wall-comment/), as well as films including Now You See Me 2, [Jurassic World: Dominion](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/scifi/jurassic-world-rebirth-release-date/) and I Came By.

**Alan Cumming as Mr Ring-a-Ding**
----------------------------------

![Image 3: Mr Ring-a-Ding, voiced by Alan Cumming, in Doctor Who season 15](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/02/Mr-Ring-a-Ding-8e33561.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Mr Ring-a-Ding, voiced by Alan Cumming, in Doctor Who season 15. BBC/Disney Plus

**Who is Mr Ring-a-Ding?** Mr Ring-a-Ding is a cartoon who lives in Sunny Town with his friend Sunshine Sally. In 1952, he springs to life as the physical form of [Lux Imperator](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lux-alan-cumming-explained/ "https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-lux-alan-cumming-explained/"), the God of Light and one of the [Pantheon of Chaos](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-pantheon-gods-explained/ "https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-pantheon-gods-explained/").

**Where have I seen Alan Cumming before?** Cumming is known for presenting The Traitors US, as well as for his roles in series including God, the Devil and Bob, Courage the Cowardly Dog, Shoebox Zoo, The L Word, Web Therapy, The Good Wife, Instinct, The Prince and Schmigadoon!.

He has also starred in films such as Goldeneye, Emma, Eyes Wide Shut, Annie, Titus, Spy Kids, Josie and the Pussycats, Burlesque and Battle of the Sexes. He played Nightcrawler in X-Men 2, a role he will be reprising in [Avengers: Doomsday](https://www.radiotimes.com/movies/scifi/avengers-5-doomsday-release-date/).

Cumming previously appeared in 2018 episode of Doctor Who, The Witchfinders, in which he played King James.

**Linus Roache as Reginald Pye**
--------------------------------

![Image 4: Linus Roache as Reginald Pye in Doctor Who, holding a can of film](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/516715-2fc04e5.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Linus Roache as Reginald Pye in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/James Pardon

**Who is Reginald Pye?** Reginald works at the Lux cinema in Miami, where the episode is set, and is grieving the loss of his beloved wife.

**Where have I seen Linus Roache before?** Roache is known for his roles in films including The Chronicles of Riddick, Batman Begins, Mandy and My Policeman, as well as series such as Kidnapped, Law & Order, [Coronation Street](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/coronation-street/), [Vikings](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/vikings-valhalla-season-3-release-date/), Summer of Rockets, Homeland, [The Recruit](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/the-recruit-season-3-release-date/), Fellow Travelers and Billy the Kid.

**Lewis Cornay as Logan Cheever**
---------------------------------

![Image 5: Lewis Cornay as Logan, Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra and Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in Doctor Who](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/516730-4c44119.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Lewis Cornay as Logan, Varada Sethu as Belinda Chandra and Ncuti Gatwa as The Doctor in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Lara Cornell

**Who is Logan Cheever?** Logan works at a diner in Miami and helps the Doctor and Belinda in their investigations into the disappearance of 15 citizens from the picturehouse.

**Where have I seen Lewis Cornay before?** Doctor Who: Lux is Cornay's first major on-screen role.

**Anita Dobson plays Mrs Flood**
--------------------------------

![Image 6: Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood in Doctor Who in a pink dressing gown](https://images.immediate.co.uk/production/volatile/sites/3/2025/04/516650-1-03acb0a.jpg?quality=90&fit=700,467)

Anita Dobson as Mrs Flood in Doctor Who. BBC Studios/Bad Wolf/Lara Cornell

**Who is Mrs Flood?** Mrs Flood is a mysterious figure, who previously posed as the next-door neighbour of the Doctor's former companion, Ruby Sunday, and most recently was seen posing as the neighbour of Belinda Chandra.

She has a habit of speaking directly to the camera, and has made many threatening assertions towards the Doctor, although he is yet to become aware of her.

Speaking with [RadioTimes.com](https://www.radiotimes.com/), showrunner Russell T Davies confirmed she is a "villain", and that she will be ["popping up every week"](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/doctor-who-mrs-flood-return-exclusive-newsupdate/) – however, we don't expect her true identity to be unveiled until later in the season.

**Where have I seen Anita Dobson before?** Dobson is best-known for playing Angie Watts in [EastEnders](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/soaps/eastenders/), while she has also appeared in series including Casualty, [Call the Midwife](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/drama/call-the-midwife-season-15-release-date/), Dodger and [Inside No 9](https://www.radiotimes.com/going-out/going-out-reviews/inside-no-9-stage-fright-review/), and took part in [Strictly Come Dancing](https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/entertainment/talent-shows/strictly-come-dancing-2024-winner-chris-mccausland/) in 2011.

**Doctor Who season 15 begins on 19th April 2025, coming to BBC iPlayer at 8am and airing at 7:15pm on BBC One.**

Ashildr
-------

Ashildr isn’t even a distant memory for the tough, uncompromising, highwaywoman that the Doctor meets in 1651…

| Fact title | Fact data |
| --- | --- |
| **Also known as:** | 
Me / Lady Me / The Knightmare / Mayor Me / Madam Mayor

 |
| **Home Planet:** | 

Earth

 |
| **First Appearance:** | 

[The Girl Who Died](https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b06kv29n)

 |
| **Latest Appearance:** | 

[Hell Bent](https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b06s609f)

 |

Having been alive for over 700 years, Ashildr - now calling herself ‘Lady Me’ - has become hardened to life. She has experienced so much and lost so many that she can’t let herself love or care again, to feel anything but indifference.

> The one and only Me. Finally, you earn the title - sitting in a reality bubble at the end of time itself.

Memories of her old life exist in diaries alone – but where the pages have been torn, the memories too painful, they have been lost forever…

The Doctor says of Ashildr, _'I saved you. I didn’t know your heart would rust because I kept it beating. I didn’t think your conscience would need renewing, that the well of human kindness would run dry. I just wanted to save a terrified young woman’s life.'_

But the Doctor knows the brave, beautiful soul he met in the Viking village is in there somewhere. He won’t let himself believe she has truly gone. And he’s right – when Me’s alliance with Leandro endangers scores of innocent people, she can’t bear it, and unites with the Doctor to save them.

When the invasion is over and the beers have been drunk, it’s clear this is no ordinary friendship…

**Me:** _…While you’re busy protecting this world, I’ll get busy protecting it from you._  
**The Doctor:** _We’re not enemies now, are we?_  
**Me:** _Of course not. Enemies are never a problem. It’s your friends you have to watch out for. And, my friend, I shall be watching out for you._

Skip forward another few centuries and Ashildr is still known as ‘Me’ - Mayor Me - the mayor of an alien refugee camp hidden in the heart of London, for those who are desperate and destitute, without hope or a home.

Ashildr’s perspective on life, her permanence, has enabled her to bring peace to a volatile refugee community – albeit under authoritarian rule with a deadly Quantum Shade. The Doctor and Clara have endangered that peace by bringing a suspected murderer back onto the street…Although the Doctor cannot condone Ashildr’s despotic style, he understands the need to find justice for Anah and her son. When Clara’s attempts to protect Rigsy lead to her death, Ashildr is devastated. Her ruse to draw the Doctor onto the street is exposed, as is the fragility of her plan… She may have succeeded in trapping the Doctor, but in underestimating the lengths to which Clara would go for a friend, she ultimately sentenced her to death.

After the death of Clara, the Doctor warns Ashildr… _I’d advise you, very strongly, to stay out of my way. You’ll find it’s a very small universe when I’m angry with you._

As it was Ashildr’s Quantum Shade that ended Clara’s life, it feels cruel, yet fitting, that Ashildr should council the Doctor about accepting her death.

**Ashildr:** _She died for who she was, and who she loved. She fell where she stood. It was sad, and it was beautiful, and it is over. We have no right to change who she was._

It is through the wisdom of Ashildr and Clara, two women whose lives are so intricately entwined with his own, that the Doctor realises he cannot continue with the path he has on - by breaking every rule in the Universe to bring Clara back, he risks falling victim to a self-fulfilling prophecy. He risks becoming the Hybrid.

The Doctor, Ashildr and Clara ultimately defeat the very idea of the Hybrid, but not without sacrifice. The strength, bravery and spirit that we saw in Ashildr as a girl comes to the fore once more, as she guides Clara back towards the day of her death… even if they do decide to go ‘the long way round’.

The Woman Who Lived
-------------------

![Image 1: Doctor Who S35 E6 "The Woman Who Lived" Recap](https://mediaproxy.tvtropes.org/width/1200/https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/the_woman_who_lived.jpg)

_"People like us, we go on too long. We forget what matters. The last thing we need is each other."_

Written by Catherine Tregenna  
Directed by Ed Bazalgette  
**Air date:** 24 October 2015  
**Part 2 of 2**

_"You didn't save my life, Doctor, you trapped me in it._"

— **Ashildr/Me**

[The one where](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/JustForFun/TheOneWith "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/JustForFun/TheOneWith") the [Jack Harkness](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/JohnBarrowman "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Creator/JohnBarrowman") [treatment](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhoWantsToLiveForever "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhoWantsToLiveForever") is gender-inverted.

And as a result, the victim subjects herself to the Doctor treatment... detaching herself from everything [and discarding her real name.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ThatManIsDead "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ThatManIsDead")

* * *

England, 1651. A carriage is travelling along a road in a forest at night, when it is accosted by a highwayman on a rearing black horse — the infamous Knightmare.

At the same time, the Doctor arrives in the woods. He's looking for some kind of alien artifact, and he has a gadget to detect it. It's somewhere nearby.

The Knightmare demands the valuables of the carriage's passengers, especially a particular amulet that the young woman in the carriage, Lucy Fanshawe, especially treasures. As the valuables are being handed over, the Doctor suddenly appears, scanning for that alien artifact. The Knightmare is not pleased that someone is interfering in his robbery, and even less pleased that the Doctor doesn't even realize that there's a robbery going on at all. The carriage takes the opportunity to escape, making the Knightmare even more annoyed. The Doctor, having realized that the person he's talking to is a robber, is also frustrated, because _he_ didn't get what he was looking for either — something called the Eye of Hades.

It's at this point that the Knightmare reveals something that catches the Doctor by surprise — "he" is actually a "she", specifically the immortal Ashildr. She takes him to her house, where she has artifacts from her eight hundred years of life, and hundreds of diaries to compensate for the limited space in her brain. She doesn't even remember her original name anymore, and has taken to calling herself simply "Me". The highway robbery is to stave off boredom.

The Doctor doesn't know it, but she's so desperate to get off Earth that she's teamed up with an alien who's promised to help her leave, no matter what the cost...
